mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the signal fails in a high-inflation environment where real rates remain negative.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the same month signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < previous month - 10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the GDP and housing weakness coincides with a strong labor market and positive earnings surprises.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate margins, which in turn drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months, or the signal fails during periods of strong productivity growth and cost-cutting cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% from the previous month, sustained for two consecutive months, signals a contraction in manufacturing output and input demand, which typically precedes negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days due to earnings downgrades.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the industrial contraction coincides with a simultaneous surge in technology sector outperformance.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) above 350k for three consecutive months, combined with a stable unemployment rate, signals a tight labor market that pressures firms to raise wages and prices, which can erode profit margins and lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 350000 for 3 consecutive months AND UNRATE stable (change < 0.1pp)
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or inflation does not accelerate as expected.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in the federal funds rate below 1% during a recession signals an aggressive monetary easing cycle, which typically boosts risk asset valuations and results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls below 1% during two consecutive quarters of negative GDP growth
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the easing fails to restore credit conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly increase of more than 2% in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and a rise in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 8% signals a synchronized expansion in consumer and housing demand, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to improved corporate earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change > 2% AND HOUST monthly change > 8%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the demand surge is accompanied by a spike in inflation that erodes real profits.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 4% for six consecutive months, coupled with stable or rising federal funds rates, signals a high-inflation environment with restrictive monetary policy, which historically has been associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to compressed real earnings.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 4% for 6 consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS stable or rising
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the inflation proves transitory and is followed by rate cuts.
